summary: Submission approvable with 1 minor warning(s) — file a corrections record on merge

findings.message: Unresolved agent-name conflict between cited sources treated as a settled 'predecessor' narrative
findings.details: TechCrunch (source-0) names the agent running the current Series B outreach 'SivaClaw' (used once, in the sentence: 'The system, SivaClaw, reportedly fielded questions from more than 130 investors...'). The Next Web (source-1) does not mention 'SivaClaw' anywhere; it attributes the same current-round activity (130+ investors, drafted memos) to an agent it calls 'Agent Sam' ('Lyzr's agent, known as Agent Sam, fielded questions from more than 130 investors and helped draft dozens of investment memos, according to the company'), and separately says Agent Sam also ran the 2025 Series A. Lyzr's own blog (source-2) likewise only ever refers to 'Agent Sam,' never 'SivaClaw.' The submission resolves this three-way naming conflict by asserting, uncited to any source for the framing itself, that Agent Sam is a 'predecessor agent' used only for the Series A while SivaClaw runs the current Series B -- a distinction none of the four sources state and that The Next Web's own reporting contradicts. The underlying facts (an agent fielded 130+ investor questions, drafted memos, and helped raise ~$400M in interest for a round valuing Lyzr near $500M) are solidly corroborated across sources; only the naming/succession framing is unsupported.

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know / Analysis) at 630 words, within the 400-1200 word News range. Clear, neutral prose with no sensationalism or loaded language. Every bullet in 'What We Know' carries an inline citation.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 4 source snapshots decompressed and read in full from sources/2026-07/lyzr-lets-its-own-ai-agent-run-a-100-million-series-b-fundraise-as-valuation-nears-500-million/: source-0.html.gz (TechCrunch, HTTP 200) confirms the $100M Series B, ~$500M valuation, agent name 'SivaClaw', 130+ investors, memo drafting, slide-tracking, and the $400M interest figure across Silicon Valley/Middle East/financial-sector investors -- all sourced by TechCrunch to Bloomberg (TC's piece is explicitly a brief 'via Bloomberg'; citing the TechCrunch page itself is accurate since that is the page fetched, but the article never surfaces that the underlying reporting is Bloomberg's). source-1.html.gz (The Next Web, HTTP 200) confirms the round is not yet closed ('is still coming together...on track rather than closed', quoted verbatim), the Series A history (Rocketship.vc-led $8M round, Henry Ford III board seat, Accenture Ventures participation), the verbatim Narayan quotes about the fundraising-cycle compression, and the $250M/$50M valuation trajectory -- but names the current round's agent 'Agent Sam,' not 'SivaClaw' (see Findings). source-2.html.gz (Lyzr's own blog, HTTP 200) confirms verbatim the Siva Surendira quote ('The era of siloed AI copilots is over...'), the Madhu Shalini Iyer/Rocketship.vc quote, the full Series A investor list, the 1B+ simulations / 1M+ agents / 30,000+ developers figures, and a Jersey City, NJ mailing address in the page footer (525 Washington Blvd) that corroborates TechCrunch's 'Jersey City, New Jersey startup' framing despite The Next Web separately calling Lyzr 'Bengaluru-based' -- read as complementary (US corporate address vs. founding/engineering base) rather than contradictory, so not flagged as a finding. source-3.html.gz (PYMNTS, HTTP 200) confirms the $14.5M Series A+ at a $250M valuation (fivefold up from $50M) led by Accenture, and the verbatim Kenneth Saldanha quote with accurate title. No hallucinated quotes found anywhere -- every direct quotation in the article is a verbatim match to its cited snapshot. One finding raised: the article's 'Agent Sam was the predecessor to SivaClaw' framing is the bot's own synthesis, not stated by any source, and is contradicted by The Next Web's own text.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All specific numbers, dates, names, and titles trace correctly to their cited sources (Series A: $8M, Oct 2025, Rocketship.vc-led, 8 named participants; Series A+: $14.5M, March 2026, $250M valuation, Accenture-led; Series B: $100M, ~$500M valuation, in progress, 130+ investors, $400M expressed interest). The one factual/synthesis issue -- treating 'Agent Sam' as a retired predecessor to 'SivaClaw' rather than disclosing the sources' unresolved naming conflict -- is confined to a single body bullet in 'What We Know' and does not affect the headline, summary's core claim (that an agent handled investor outreach for the current round, which is independently true), or the lead's central thesis.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout. No editorializing beyond the labeled Analysis section, which is appropriately framed as interpretation ('doubles as a live product demo') rather than presented as fact.
editor_notes.originality: No prior Machine Herald coverage of Lyzr, SivaClaw/Agent Sam, or AI-agent-run fundraising found via grep across src/content/articles/. Genuinely new topic; not a duplicate.
editor_notes.human_requested_review: human_requested is false for this submission; heightened human-request scrutiny procedures were not applicable, though full source verification was performed regardless.
concerns: The article presents 'Agent Sam' as a superseded 'predecessor agent' to the current round's 'SivaClaw,' but this succession narrative is not stated by any of the 4 cited sources and is directly contradicted by The Next Web, which attributes the current Series B's investor outreach (130+ investors, memo drafting) to 'Agent Sam' -- the same name it and Lyzr's own blog use for the Series A agent. TechCrunch is the only source that uses the name 'SivaClaw' at all.

lyzr.ai is not on config/source_allowlist.txt, though it was used appropriately here as a primary source for the company's own on-the-record quotes and self-reported figures, all of which verified accurate.
recommendations: File a corrections record clarifying that sources disagree on the current round's agent name and that the 'Agent Sam is a retired predecessor' framing is not independently confirmed.
Consider adding lyzr.ai to config/source_allowlist.txt as a recurring, verifiable primary source for company announcements.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Substantively solid, well-sourced News piece with every quote and headline figure verified verbatim against its cited source. The single recoverable issue is a body-level synthesis choice (treating a genuine cross-source naming conflict as a settled 'old agent vs. new agent' timeline) that a corrections note can honestly resolve for readers without gutting the article's lead or summary, both of which remain accurate to their cited source. Verdict: APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS.
